title: An adjunction unit telescope detects equality at a scalar power
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a preadditive category [def-weil-preadditive-category], let $\mathcal B$ be a category, and fix an adjunction $F:\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:U$ with unit $\eta$ (thus $\operatorname{Hom}(FA,T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,UT)$ naturally). Fix $a\in\mathbf N$ and objects $K,B\in\mathcal A$. Let $t$ be a cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] on the sequence $B\xrightarrow{a\operatorname{id}}B\to\cdots$, with vertex $UFB$ and zeroth leg $\eta_B$. Suppose that postcomposition with its legs exhibits $\operatorname{Hom}(K,UFB)$ as the colimit in abelian groups of the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(K,B)\xrightarrow{a}\operatorname{Hom}(K,B)\to\cdots$. Then, for any $f,g:K\to B$, the equality $F(f)=F(g)$ implies $a^nf=a^ng$ for some $n\geq0$. All sequences are indexed by a small copy of $\mathbf N$.

source.place: Full faithfulness; adjunction and finite-stage equality, expanded by the agent

proof.text: Write $t_i:B\to UFB$ for the cocone legs and $q_i:\operatorname{Hom}(K,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,UFB)$ for $h\mapsto t_i\circ h$. Naturality of the given unit, applied to $f$ and $g$, gives $\eta_B\circ f=UF(f)\circ\eta_K=UF(g)\circ\eta_K=\eta_B\circ g$, since $F(f)=F(g)$. As $t_0=\eta_B$, this is $q_0(f)=q_0(g)$. This is substitution in the defining naturality square; neither functor is assumed additive.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and the following paragraph: the adjunction maps form natural transformations; applied to the blueprint Full faithfulness paragraph

proof.text: Let $H_i=\operatorname{Hom}(K,B)$ at every index, with each successor map multiplication by $a$. By preadditivity, the $H_i$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(K,UFB)$ are abelian groups, and the $q_i$ are homomorphisms: $q_i(h+h\prime)=t_i\circ(h+h\prime)=q_i(h)+q_i(h\prime)$. The cocone identity for $t$ gives $q_{i+1}(ah)=q_i(h)$. The hypothesis is precisely that these $q_i$ form a colimit cocone in abelian groups. The small ordered category $\mathbf N$ is filtered: it is nonempty, two indices have upper bound their maximum, and parallel arrows are equal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-groups-forget-filtered-colimits] to obtain a colimit cocone of underlying sets, with the same vertex and the same maps $q_i$. Choose a universe containing the two Hom groups and the small index category.

source.place: Full faithfulness, the displayed Hom-colimit comparison: passage from its assumed abelian-group colimit to the underlying-set colimit; the cited preservation leaf supplies this step

proof.text: Apply clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] to this underlying-set colimit and to the two elements $f,g\in H_0$. The equality $q_0(f)=q_0(g)$ from step 1 gives an index $n$ and the unique arrow $0\to n$ for which $H(0\to n)(f)=H(0\to n)(g)$. This uses the same-index equality clause; no surjectivity or injectivity of a particular cocone leg is assumed.

source.place: Tag 04AX, section-directed-colimits, description of the equivalence relation after Definition 002V; equality at a common stage, applied at index zero

proof.text: For every $h\in\operatorname{Hom}(K,B)$, induction on $n$ computes $H(0\to n)(h)=a^n h$: for $n=0$ the transition is the identity and $a^0h=1h=h$; for $n+1$ functoriality of the sequence and its specified successor map give $H(0\to n+1)(h)=aH(0\to n)(h)=a(a^n h)=a^{n+1}h$. The scalar identity follows by distributing the finite repeated sums in the abelian Hom group. Substitution in step 3 gives $a^n f=a^n g$ for the index $n\geq0$ found there. This induction also covers $a=0$ (including $n=0$) and $a=1$.

source.place: Full faithfulness: finite-stage equality for the repeated scalar diagram, expanded by induction
